requirements.statement: M16 node-to-node supervision shall use a contract distinct from Guardian Protocol v0.1 host/device command semantics.
Successful node authentication shall not directly grant physical actuation authority.
Within one initialized runtime session, NodeLink shall reject duplicate or regressing sequence values.
Loss of the supervisory link shall resolve through a deterministic bounded local state and shall not silently increase authority.
Disagreement between the STM32F401 node and the NXP supervisory node shall not silently grant unilateral authority to either node.
NodeLink core semantics shall remain independent of UART, SPI, CAN, CAN-FD or other physical transport adapters.
NodeLink CRC integrity shall not be represented as cryptographic authentication.
Host validation of M16 NodeLink shall not be promoted to evidence of physical dual-node hardware behavior.

Interpretation of trust-, authority-, safety-, supervision- or actuation-relevant node information shall be bound to the applicable node identity, chip family, hardware revision, firmware or platform version, protocol version, semantic profile and system role where those dimensions can alter meaning.
Protocol compatibility or identical field names shall not be treated as proof of semantic equivalence across chip families, platform revisions, firmware versions or semantic profiles.

A material change in the meaning of a state, field, command, capability, error or authority-relevant signal shall establish an explicit versioned semantic change boundary preserving prior meaning and identifying the new effective profile.

Historical semantic records shall not be silently reinterpreted using later semantic profiles; prior meaning, decision context and change boundaries shall remain reconstructible for audit and forensic review.
Cross-node compatibility shall be explicitly version-bound; wire or protocol compatibility alone shall not authorize semantic compatibility.

Unknown, ambiguous, unsupported or historically impossible platform-version-semantic-profile combinations shall not be guessed for authority-, trust-, safety-, supervision- or actuation-relevant decisions and shall resolve to an explicitly bounded fail-safe or fail-closed behavior.
Registration of a document or semantic artifact shall represent governed identity or integrity only and shall not by itself imply APPROVED, IMPLEMENTED, VALIDATED or EVIDENCE_PRESENT status.
Unauthorized semantic drift, including silent reinterpretation of historically governed fields or platform meanings, shall be detected as a governance or validation failure.
